projectTitle: MycoVela — helping mycorrhizal fungi establish with plants in lunar regolith simulant
tagline: Protect arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi from the oxidative chemistry of lunar regolith so they can form symbiosis with crops off Earth.
summary: Lunar regolith generates hydroxyl radicals and stunts plant growth, and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) are the obvious partner to help plants reach nutrients in it — if the spores survive long enough to germinate. MycoVela tests whether pyomelanin, catalase, trehalose and calcium alginate can protect AMF during establishment in regolith simulant. The dry lab is a five-part collection built by a Boys and Girls Club team drawing students from ten schools, and its statistical standard is genuinely graduate-level: a 34-parameter Monte Carlo oxidative-stress simulation, a Fisher-information identifiability and Sobol sensitivity analysis that found exact degeneracies and an unobservable parameter and so changed the model's own equations, a hierarchical Bayesian dose-response model with partial pooling across three laboratories and 400 simulation-based calibration runs, a reproducible image-analysis tool (MycoLens) whose failure cases are published alongside its successes, and a structural screen of KatE catalase surface variants.

dry.frameworks: Five distinct computational pieces, each answering a different question, and the chain between them is the real achievement. MODEL-03, the Oxidative Stress and AMF Protection Model, is a Monte Carlo simulation over 34 biological parameters covering side-reaction kinetics, reactive-oxygen-species regeneration and antioxidant effects, predicting AMF germination (24 h) and hyphal development (240 h) under a declared lunar stress scenario phi. Treatments are compared under the SAME sampled conditions, which is what makes the probabilistic comparison meaningful, and the model is built around real mechanism: vitamin C is a strong scavenger of hydroxyl radical and superoxide but reacts slowly with peroxide and reduces Fe(III) to Fe(II), feeding the Fenton reaction, so the model weighs protection against that side reaction; pyomelanin by contrast coats the regolith and reduces stress at source but binds iron. The headline output is a trade-off rather than a winner: pyomelanin protects germination more strongly than vitamin C in 61-76% of parameter draws under every variation of the ranges, but reduces hyphal growth at high doses in 17-50% of draws. MODEL-04, the Measurement Design Model, is the standout. It takes MODEL-03's own equations and asks which parameters the planned measurements can actually distinguish: it computes the sensitivity matrix S, forms the Fisher information matrix F = S^T S, and counts how many parameter combinations a measurement panel determines to within +/-10% (eigenvalues of F above 1/0.1^2) and +/-30%; it separately finds the largest identifiable subset by greedy search under a collinearity index threshold gamma <= 15, and reports both because the greedy subset need not grow when measurements are added while the Fisher count must. Candidate exact degeneracies are not merely asserted but VERIFIED numerically by moving the model 10% along each direction and measuring the change in every observation — exact if under 0.001 standard deviations, against a benchmark that a genuine 10% change in one parameter moves observations by about one SD. Three exact degeneracies were confirmed with their mechanism named (k_fen and f_pH appear only as a product in the Fenton term; p_max and pi_pH only as a product in the germination map; growth sees only Fe_tot/K_N while Fenton chemistry sees only Fe_tot*k_fen). Run on MODEL-03's ORIGINAL parameterisation it also flagged R_0 and phi_sim as exactly confounded, which, with the analytical result that k_dmg, D_50 and D_g50 act only through their ratios, is why the team fixed the damage scale and demoted phi_sim to a declared scenario — a model changed by its own identifiability analysis. Total-order Sobol indices from 512 base samples complement the local analysis, with damage analysed on a log scale because on the original scale 1% of samples carried 89% of the variance. Final verdict: of 34 parameters, 13 identifiable alone, 8 only with a correlated partner, 6 structurally confounded, 6 weakly sensitive, and one (rho_root) unobservable. MODEL-05, the Bayesian Dose-Response Model, fits protection and toxicity curves with a hierarchical model that lets the three collaborating laboratories (UCI, Chapman, Sino American Cancer Foundation) have different protection EC50 values via partial pooling, ec50_s = ec50_pop * exp(ec50_site_sd * z_s) with z_s ~ N(0,1), estimating the between-site standard deviation from the data rather than fixing it. An ordered transform constrains the protection curve to be non-decreasing, and the team state plainly that this is a LIMITATION they cannot fix within the model: if colonization rose and then fell at high dose the model could not represent it, and the separate plant-toxicity likelihood would not repair the missing decline — and they note MODEL-03 predicts exactly that shape on mechanistic grounds, so the two models are in productive tension. MycoLens measures fungal geometry from microscopy images by building a pixel graph and skeletonising it to extract hyphal length and junction nodes. The KatE screen is a structural-bioinformatics design: starting from E. coli KatE/HPII (UniProt P21179, 753 residues; PDB 28WU four-subunit structure, chosen over KatG/HPI and B. subtilis KatA), it excludes positions 1-509 as a conservative rule, then requires every candidate site to pass, in all four subunits, relative solvent accessibility >= 0.35 (Biopython Shrake-Rupley, 1.4 Angstrom probe, 300 sphere points per atom, Tien maximum-accessibility values), <= 5 Angstrom^2 accessibility lost on tetramer assembly, >= 25 Angstrom from heme, >= 10 Angstrom from another chain, >= 20 Angstrom from protected sites and >= 4 Angstrom between basic side-chain nitrogens and acidic oxygens; six variants were modelled in PyMOL 3.2.0a with low-strain rotamers and cross-checked against a five-homolog panel (P30266, P42234, P50979, P95539, Q9X576), selecting K624E primary and K621E backup, with the double substitution deliberately deferred 'to keep the first comparison interpretable'. MycoFerre, the radiation-transport side of the hardware, uses NIST attenuation and stopping-power tables with referenced material properties.
dry.dataviz: Figures are built to answer design questions, not to look impressive. Figure 4.2 is a measurement-by-parameter sensitivity heatmap where darker means the measurement responds more strongly and is therefore more useful for estimating that parameter — and the caption reads the pattern for you (germination responds to stress and damage parameters, hyphal length to growth parameters, peroxide and superoxide to pigment chemistry, surface coverage weakly to everything). Figure 4.3 shows the identifiability of all 34 parameters grouped by class with a sensitivity floor drawn as a dashed line. Figure 4.4 is the one that changed the experiment: cumulative measurement panels ordered by assumed effort, showing germination alone determines only two parameter combinations to +/-30%, adding the hyphal time course raises it to five, adding peroxide to ten (the largest single gain), superoxide and residual pigment add one each, and surface coverage adds nothing. Figure 4.5 ranks measurements by information added AND by information lost if dropped, which is a different and more useful question. Figure 5.1 plots protection and toxicity curves on one dose axis with 94% credible bands and shades the safe window where both criteria hold (at least 0.10 gain in colonization over control and under 0.10 additional plant damage). Figure 5.6 draws the shape the model CANNOT fit next to the shape it can. Figure 5.9 compares each laboratory fitted independently against the pooled fit and reports that all three shifts are under 0.5 mg/plant and well inside their credible intervals, so with this much data the pooling choice barely matters. Table 5.3 is a prior-by-prior evidence table. The MycoLens image pilot is a published failure report: original, mask and skeleton-plus-junction overlays side by side, with draft reference traces in magenta against MycoLens skeletons in cyan, and the numbers that disagree stated outright (skeleton 3,195 um versus draft trace 500 um on one frame; 1,139 versus 437 on another; 12 um of skeleton produced from background debris in a region with no visible hyphae).
dry.datascience: The epistemic discipline here exceeds most undergraduate entries. MODEL-03 was deliberately NOT calibrated to the team's own laboratory data, and they say why and what that costs: absolute predictions depend on literature-estimated ranges, so 'the rankings describe the chosen equations and ranges' and 'their stability across the tested variations does not establish the ranking in AMF experiments'. Pyomelanin doses are labelled explicitly as model-equivalent scenario coordinates with no molecular-mass or repeat-unit basis, so the apparent sixtyfold potency gap against vitamin C 'cannot be converted into experimental doses or compared as a measured potency difference' — a unit-honesty most teams skip. The calibration procedure itself was checked against synthetic germination counts with known truth. MODEL-05's validation is textbook Bayesian workflow: parameter recovery on simulated colonization and plant-damage counts, 400 simulation-based calibration runs, 14 prior-sensitivity fits and nine pooling comparisons, with a DELIBERATELY BROKEN equation used to demonstrate why parameter recovery is needed in addition to convergence checks — because a wrong model can still converge. MCMC is four chains, 1500 tuning steps and 1500 draws each at target acceptance 0.9, with a hard gate of R-hat below 1.01, bulk and tail effective sample size above 400, and zero divergences, judged on the worst diagnostic across all eight parameters, followed by the line that matters: 'Passing is a prerequisite for interpretation; it does not show that the biological model is correct.' Table 5.3 grades every prior by its evidence: two rest on a genuine quantitative literature base (Hill slopes from Prinz and Schonichen 2008 and Prinz 2010, chosen over a HalfNormal because that peaks at zero and would make 'no dose-response at all' the most likely shape), two on one-sided bounds from studies that never measured the needed quantity, one qualitative only, and four on reasoning and bounds alone — and they point out that the two parameters which most strongly determine the final recommendation, EC50 and tox_EC50, are among the least well evidenced. They further identify a unit-conversion blocker: every published figure is in mg/L while their dose axis is mg/plant, the conversion needs an applied volume that is not recorded, so both priors currently fall back to scaling from the configured maximum dose — and 'the model reports which basis is in force on every run rather than concealing the fallback'. The ec50_site_sd prior is deliberately wide because with only three sites the between-site SD is weakly identified and 'a tighter prior would manufacture false confidence in site similarity'. MycoLens was verified against eleven hand-defined skeletons at three calibrations and on degraded synthetic images, then run on three public fungal-colony crops WITHOUT retuning — and the results are reported as failures where they failed: default dark Otsu masks followed background texture, particle edges and phase halos; the frozen S1 preset (bright adaptive threshold, 51 px window, offset 15, minimum component 30 px) left disconnected fragments and missed faint strands; settings were tuned on one movie (S1) with S2 and S3 held out and all frames from a movie kept together to avoid leakage; input JPEGs were checked against Zenodo MD5 checksums; and the honest conclusion is that 'these comparisons do not establish biological measurement accuracy' because the missing reference is human agreement, for which they built a blank two-reviewer tracing workspace that presents the same nine regions with no model overlays or AI traces so independent polylines can be compared spatially as well as by total length. They also note that a similar total length can hide completely different traced structures. An independent check against published growth data (Serghi et al. 2021, 219 spores across nine strains, CC BY 4.0) is flagged as extending beyond MODEL-03's configured 240-hour horizon.
dry.software: Everything is built for reuse by other teams. Each model keeps treatment inputs, shared parameter ranges and run settings in separate files with source notes for every value, and the exact run configuration is published: 0.05 h default step, 3,000 germination draws, 800 hyphal-length draws, seed 20260809. MycoLens saves the input hash, settings and calibration with every measurement, pins its source version and exact dependencies, gives the commands to reproduce each validation figure, and carries a recorded test suite of 99 tests; the pilot analysis names its exact build (MycoLens 2.0, commit 1e030449). The team state the reuse limitation that matters most: the Bayesian model's protection curve cannot describe a decline at high dose, and MycoLens's default segmentation performs poorly on images with different characteristics, so a team using it on new specimens would need to check the masks and validate against reference annotations. Model documentation is also published as a PDF. Two games, Lunar Traitor and MycoVela: Lunar Lab, plus a transport simulator and 3D designs, carry the science into lessons. A U-Net segmentation pipeline exists but is explicitly untrained pending annotated AMF images.

good.publicEngagement: An outstanding programme for a club-based team. Genesis brought students from ten schools together through the Boys and Girls Club of Fullerton, and over 80% of the schools in their ten-lesson programme were Title I schools, with free after-school and home participation. Across seven school and club locations children used micropipettes, tested protective structures and designed organisms with safety switches; the seven planned lessons became nine. Outcomes are measured and reported with numbers: 83% of Speaker Series respondents reported learning about synthetic biology and 95% wanted to return; across two high-school lessons 82.5% reported greater interest in synthetic biology and 77.3% said they would seek further research opportunities; at Discovery Cube the proportion rating their space-agriculture knowledge highly rose from 26.7% to 86.7%; at Rocket Fever 95.5% reported learning more about space agriculture. Activities include a Moon Farm Challenge, a Save the Moon Plant model and hands-on roots-and-AMF models, plus two original games. Individual learners are spotlighted by name and story rather than counted (Ryan sharing his designs at Speaker Series, Cora teaching her parents at Discovery Cube, Anya explaining fungal networks over Zoom).
good.ihp: Structured as four repeating steps — Aspiration, Action, Analysis, Adaptation — with each cycle starting from a question, recording the feedback received, and explaining what was done with it, then linking that decision to the specific experimental plan, model, design or activity it changed. The team are explicit that some conversations made them let an idea go, and they name which: Robertas Ursache's feedback led them away from CIF peptides, Julie Brisset changed how they planned their regolith mixtures, and Ian Sanders pushed them to look more closely at moisture and spore germination. A stakeholder assessment table matches each question to relevant expertise across six perspectives — plant and space biology (Marzan, Ursache, Blancaflor, Sanders, Levy, Berliner), regolith and lunar systems (Horanyi, Amoros Trepat, Brisset, Yong), safety and future use (Kutz, Demick, Fulmer, Exponent), educators and families, design and reuse, and prospective users — and, unusually, it also tracks which perspectives their records do NOT yet cover. Dr Florian Schunck advised on using leave-one-out validation and WAIC to compare alternative model structures, and Dr Marco Bisoffi of Chapman served as scientific advisor; the honesty extends to the business side, where they write that 'confirmed adoption and purchasing decisions remain to be demonstrated'.
good.realWorld: The scientific case is built on cited evidence rather than enthusiasm: Hendrix et al. (2024) found experimentally reduced lunar simulants generated roughly 5 to 100 times more hydroxyl radicals in deionized water than non-reduced simulants, linked to metallic iron from reduction; Paul et al. (2022) grew Arabidopsis in Apollo 11, 12 and 17 regolith and found about 71% of differentially expressed genes associated with salt, metal or ROS stress, with the most mature sample (Apollo 11) producing the slowest growth; Atkin et al. (2026) showed an AMF inoculum let chickpeas set seed in up to 75% LHS-1 simulant but not in 100%, where plants were colonised and survived two weeks longer yet died without flowering. The commercial plan is deliberately terrestrial first and candid about what it needs: it targets nursery and transplant growers, and the team state they 'will need to find a crop and stress condition where adding the carrier improves on existing inoculants', that potential use in degraded soil would require separate work, and that they would simplify the formulation if fewer components work just as well. Cost per treatment is published.

images.caption: Figure 4.2: sensitivity of each planned measurement to each of the 34 model parameters. Darker cells mean the measurement responds more strongly and is therefore more useful for estimating that parameter — germination tracks the stress and damage parameters, hyphal length the growth parameters, peroxide and superoxide the pigment chemistry, and surface coverage almost nothing.

Figure 5.1: protection and toxicity curves on the same dose axis with 94% credible bands from the hierarchical Bayesian model. A dose enters the safe window only where both criteria hold — at least a 0.10 gain in colonization over control and under 0.10 additional plant damage — so the recommendation is a window, not a number.

Table 5.3: every prior in the Bayesian model with the evidence behind it, graded. Only two rest on a quantitative literature base; two rest on one-sided bounds from studies that never measured the quantity needed, one is qualitative, and four rest on reasoning alone — including the two parameters that most strongly determine the final dose recommendation.

Figure 11.1: MycoLens output on a public fungal-colony image — original, mask, and overlay with the extracted skeleton in red and junction nodes in yellow. The team ran the tool on public images without retuning and published where it failed, noting the colony is not AMF and that these comparisons do not establish biological measurement accuracy.

gemsTakeaway: Before you fit anything, run an identifiability analysis on your own model: build the sensitivity matrix, form the Fisher information matrix, count how many parameter combinations each candidate measurement panel can actually pin down, and verify suspected degeneracies numerically by perturbing along them. BGCFullerton used exactly this to discover that germination alone constrained two parameter combinations while adding peroxide raised it to ten — changing both their equations and the wet lab's data request — and they pair it with a prior-by-prior evidence table that grades how much each number is really known. Both are achievable by high-school students and are worth more than a larger simulation.
